newsitem.title: UK: BRAZIL 97/98 SUGAR EXPORTS COULD FALL UNDER QUOTA.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL 97/98 SUGAR EXPORTS COULD FALL UNDER QUOTA.

text.p: Brazil could have an export potential of around six million tonnes of sugar raw value in 1997/98 and so leave a portion of the official quota unused, Czarnikow Sugar said in a report on Thursday.

The export quota of 7.06 million tonnes tel quel of sugar, reported last month, was probably equivalent to between 7.30 and 7.40 million tonnes raw value but would depend on the eventual split between whites and raws.
So if there was a shift in the alcohol balance in favour of sugar there could be an increase in the forecast of actual exports with no need for additional authority to ship.

Czarnikow forecast a modest expansion in consumption after the surge seen in 1996 which limited export volumes. Brazilian consumption was forecast at 9.50 million tonnes for 1997, rising to 9.65 million for 1998.
"Exports for the whole of the 1997/98 season are likely to advance once again after being held in check the previous season," the report said.
In its first estimate of supply and demand for world sugar in 1997/98, Czarnikow pegged Brazilian sugar production at 15.50 million tonnes raw value after 14.78 million tonnes in 1996/97.
